projects.title: Async Document Pipeline
projects.summary: A document-processing work sample that keeps uploads responsive while background workers process jobs and report progress to a review UI.
projects.problem: Long-running document work should not hold an HTTP request open or leave users guessing about job state.
projects.ownership: Built the FastAPI API, Celery worker flow, PostgreSQL job model, Redis-backed SSE updates, Docker Compose stack, and backend tests.
projects.architecture: FastAPI records a document and queues work; Celery updates durable job state in PostgreSQL and publishes lifecycle events; an SSE endpoint relays progress to the Next.js UI.
projects.validation: Covers API and worker state transitions with tests, including missing documents and forced worker failures. Alembic migrations and Compose health checks make the local stack reproducible.
projects.limitation: The extraction steps currently return mock data. The repository explicitly identifies missing production work: idempotent upload requests, a dead-letter path, queue backpressure, and replayable SSE events.

projects.title: Predictive Maintenance: Cost-Aware Evaluation
projects.summary: A reproducible study of failure-risk models that evaluates maintenance decisions with calibration, cross-validation, and an explicit cost model instead of accuracy alone.
projects.problem: A high-accuracy classifier can still be operationally useless on rare failures; model and threshold choices need a defensible decision rule.
projects.ownership: Built a layered Python evaluation pipeline with physics-derived features, censored Weibull estimation, probabilistic and tree models, cost analysis, tests, and committed experiment records.
projects.architecture: Frozen configuration objects, dataset loaders, model factories, repeated stratified cross-validation, recorded JSON results, and a cost curve calculated only from held-out fold predictions.
projects.validation: On the stated 10:1:0.5 missed-failure, false-alarm, inspection cost ratio, 5×5 CV produced 0.0826 ± 0.0137 cost per row for the depth-limited tree and 0.0817 ± 0.0124 for XGBoost. The small difference supported the pre-registered finding that added model complexity did not materially change modeled cost here.
projects.limitation: This is a dataset-specific, exploratory modeled result, not a field-validated savings claim. The cost-optimal thresholds are selected from the same cross-validation predictions used for reporting, so they are not an independent deployment estimate.

projects.title: KOmpiler
projects.summary: An Android compiler playground for a small Pascal-like language, from source editing through execution and source-aware diagnostics.
projects.problem: Make compiler concepts inspectable in a mobile app without reducing the language pipeline to a black box.
projects.ownership: Implemented the handwritten lexer, recursive-descent parser, AST, semantic checks, IR generator, interpreter, source mapping, and Compose-based compiler UI.
projects.architecture: Source is tokenized, parsed into an AST, checked against a symbol table, lowered to KOmpiler IR v1, then interpreted in-app with IR-to-source mappings for diagnostics.
projects.validation: Unit tests execute a compiled factorial program and verify failures such as missing input and division by zero resolve to useful source-line diagnostics.
projects.limitation: The language intentionally has a lightweight semantic model: no full nested lexical scoping or richer type system yet.

projects.title: track-At.
projects.summary: An offline attendance companion that turns a weekly timetable and class records into actionable attendance planning.
projects.problem: Attendance tracking needs durable local data, schedule-aware workflows, and a way to recover or transfer a student’s data.
projects.ownership: Built the Kotlin app around Jetpack Compose, Room, Hilt, Navigation Compose, attendance repositories, schema migrations, and import/export support.
projects.architecture: Room entities and DAOs model semesters, subjects, sessions, and attendance records; repositories coordinate schedule and backup flows; the Compose UI uses MVVM and Hilt.
projects.validation: The public repository includes Room migration code, release builds, and product screenshots covering the dashboard, schedule, day view, and import/export experience.
projects.limitation: The portfolio will describe the implemented offline product behavior. It will not imply adoption, retention, or accuracy metrics that are not publicly evidenced.
